name: Black Saturn
description: A black ring turning in balance around a spherical black hole in five dimensions, the exact vacuum solution Henriette Elvang and Pau Figueras built in 2007 by the inverse scattering method. Rotation alone holds the two apart, each drags the other around, and one mass and angular momentum can be shared between them in a continuum of ways.
convention: The spacetime has five dimensions, with $G$ Newton's constant there. We keep factors of $c$ explicit, and the Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: Two black holes left to themselves fall together, so how could a pair of them be held apart for good [elvang2007]? In four dimensions the simplest answer is electric charge: load each hole until the repulsion cancels the attraction and any number of them stay put, the static holes of Sudhansu Datta Majumdar and Achilles Papapetrou [elvang2007, majumdar1947, papapetrou1947]. Spin fails at it: set two of Kerr's rotating holes on one axis, the double Kerr solution of 1980, and the pull between their spins is too weak to balance their attraction, so the pair stays apart only on a strut, a line of conical singularity that carries the pressure between them [elvang2007, kramer1980].¶Five dimensions hold a second kind of black hole, a ring: Roberto Emparan and Harvey Reall's solution of 2002 has a horizon that is a circle times a 2-sphere, and its own rotation keeps it from collapsing [emparan2002, elvang2007]. A very thin ring balances as a spinning hoop does, by what Henriette Elvang, Emparan, and Amitabh Virmani called "a Newtonian competition between a string-like tension and a centrifugal force" [elvang2006]. So could a ring that holds itself open also circle something? The answer came in January 2007 from Elvang and Pau Figueras: an exact solution of the vacuum equations in which a black ring turns in balance around a spherical black hole at its centre, which they named black Saturn [elvang2007].¶They made it out of a simpler solution by algebra [elvang2007]. The method is inverse scattering, which Vladimir Belinski and Vladimir Zakharov brought to gravity in 1978: for a metric that depends on two coordinates alone Einstein's vacuum equations can be integrated, and solitons added to a known solution make a new one [elvang2007, belinskii1978, belinskii1979]. The known one here is static and fits on a line, $$G_0 = \mathrm{diag}\left\{-\frac{\mu_1\mu_3}{\mu_2\mu_4},\ \frac{\rho^2\mu_4}{\mu_3\mu_5},\ \frac{\mu_2\mu_5}{\mu_1}\right\}, \qquad \mu_i = \sqrt{\rho^2 + (z - a_i)^2} - (z - a_i),$$ a ring and a hole at rest and one rod of negative density, with five rod ends $a_i$ on the axis of Weyl's coordinates $\rho$ and $z$ [elvang2007]. Elvang and Figueras took three solitons out of it and put them back turned, as Andrei Pomeransky had done to derive the Myers-Perry black hole of five dimensions, and fixed one constant so that the singularity left at one rod end disappeared [elvang2007, pomeransky2006]. The metric that came out is long enough that they checked it by computer: "We have resorted to numerical methods in order to check the vanishing of all components of the Ricci tensor" [elvang2007].¶A ring spinning around a hole pulls the hole round with it: give the hole no angular momentum of its own and its horizon turns all the same, at an angular velocity that follows the ring's, which Elvang and Figueras took to be the dragging of frames, "the rotating black ring drags the spacetime around with it" [elvang2007]. They tested the reading by moving the ring away, and the hole's rotation died off with the distance [elvang2007]. Spin the hole against the ring by the right amount and its horizon stands still though it carries angular momentum [elvang2007]. When ring and hole turn the same way their two ergoregions, where nothing can stand still against the rotation, can join into one, a merger that Elvang, Figueras, Gary Horowitz, Veronika Hubeny, and Mukund Rangamani followed through in 2008 [elvang2009].¶Spin the hole harder still against the ring and the total angular momentum comes to zero while the two stay in balance [elvang2007]. From far away such a Saturn has a mass and no angular momentum, as Frank Tangherlini's static hole has, so in five dimensions, Elvang and Figueras wrote, "the 4+1d Schwarzschild black hole is not unique" [elvang2007, tangherlini1963]. Gary Gibbons, Daisuke Ida, and Tetsuya Shiromizu had proved that the static hole is the only static black hole of the vacuum that is flat far away, and the theorem stands, since a Saturn is stationary and its two parts turn [elvang2007, gibbons2002]. For a given mass and angular momentum the two can be shared between ring and hole in a continuum of ways, "2-fold continuous non-uniqueness" [elvang2007]. In February 2007 Elvang, Emparan, and Figueras argued that at every mass and angular momentum the arrangement of greatest entropy is a Saturn, with nearly all the mass in a central hole that hardly turns and the spin in a long thin ring [elvang2007phases].¶Is such a metric really a black hole spacetime, smooth and free of closed timelike curves outside its horizons? Piotr Chruściel, Michał Eckstein, and Sebastian Szybka settled the first half in 2010: the metric extends smoothly across two separate event horizons, one whose sections are 3-spheres and one whose sections are a circle times a 2-sphere [chrusciel2010]. The rod end where the constant had been fixed is, they showed, a smooth point of the spacetime like any other, a "ghost point" in their words [chrusciel2010]. For the second half Szybka proved that the region outside the horizons is stably causal, which rules out closed timelike curves there [szybka2011]. Whether a Saturn is stable is open: a thin ring is expected to ripple as a black string does, and of a ring close to its hole Emparan and Reall wrote in 2008, "We know essentially nothing about what happens when the gravitational interactions among the black objects involved is strong" [emparan2008].

related.text: Black Saturn with its ring taken away. In the limit $\kappa_3 \to \kappa_2$ and then $\kappa_2 \to 0$ the ring's horizon shrinks to nothing and leaves the Myers-Perry black hole with one spin [elvang2007].

The static black hole of five dimensions. A Saturn whose hole turns against its ring can have the same mass and no angular momentum at infinity, so those two numbers do not single it out [elvang2007].
A thin black ring is a black string bent into a circle and set spinning. It is expected to share the string's Gregory-Laflamme instability [elvang2006, elvang2007].
Black holes held apart by electric charge, in four dimensions. Saturn's ring and hole carry no charge, and rotation does the holding [elvang2007].
The method that made black Saturn. Belinski and Zakharov found it in 1978 in four dimensions, where two solitons on flat space are Kerr's black hole [belinskii1978, belinskii1979].

The functions $V$, $\Omega$, $W$, and $\nu$ stand free in every component, and no component assumes a field equation. parameters.description: Length that sets the scale ($L > 0$): the mass, the angular momentum and every radius are fixed multiples of its powers
